channel.title: NewsCenter — All newsletter news — 2026-11-14
channel.description: Every news received through Laurent's newsletters over the last 24 hours. 54 news received.

item.title: A software update reportedly caused flights to stop across the United States
item.description: An update to L3Harris’s private network reportedly caused communications used by U.S. air traffic control to fail. The FAA lifted the flight stoppage after more than four hours, but delays are expected to continue for several days.

item.title: Starship reaches orbit despite its booster exploding
item.description: The Starship spacecraft reached orbit on its 15th test flight and deployed 26 Starlink satellites. The Super Heavy booster failed during its return and exploded in the Gulf of Mexico.

item.title: The Tesla Cybercab requires a $299 monthly subscription
item.description: Tesla has started selling the Cybercab for $29,990 to a few customers in the Austin area. The vehicle cannot operate without a $299-per-month Autonomy subscription, and its use is limited by several restrictions.

item.title: OpenAI dissolves its dedicated robotics team
item.description: OpenAI is transferring its robotics researchers to its main research group and its applied staff to Greg Brockman’s organization. The company believes general-purpose models such as GPT-6 Astra can directly control robots.

item.title: Anthropic’s IPO is reportedly oversubscribed sixfold
item.description: Anthropic’s IPO is reportedly oversubscribed sixfold and could become the largest in history.

item.title: AI risks are the biggest threat to the financial system
item.description: A Federal Reserve survey finds that artificial intelligence risks are considered the biggest threat to the financial system.

item.title: Cloudflare open-sources its Kitesurf browser engine
item.description: Cloudflare has open-sourced Kitesurf, a browser engine designed for artificial intelligence agents.

item.title: Study examines AI safety issues affecting children
item.description: A research paper examines children’s safety in relation to artificial intelligence systems.

item.title: Amazon wants to control product data to counter AI shopping agents
item.description: Amazon is reportedly preparing a strategy to control product data and combat shopping agents powered by artificial intelligence.

item.title: Business Insider highlights 20 young real estate figures
item.description: Real estate is being transformed by lawsuits over agent commissions, changes at listing websites, evolving tax rules and artificial intelligence. Business Insider selected 20 people under 35 who are playing an important role in these changes.

item.title: Chinese Supplier Confirms Its Involvement in Unreleased Apple Products
item.description: An Apple supplier in China appears to have confirmed its involvement in Apple’s AI glasses, camera-equipped AirPods and other unannounced projects in a financial report.

item.title: OLED iPad Air Expected in Early 2027
item.description: A new report claims that the iPad Air with an OLED display will arrive in early 2027. It is not expected to support ProMotion.

item.title: Government-Grade Spyware Is Now Targeting iPhones
item.description: Researchers say sophisticated spyware previously reserved for government surveillance is being used against private individuals. Two iOS exploit kits, Coruna and DarkSword, are involved.

item.title: OLED iPad mini Review: An Excellent Reader, but Not a Miniature iPad Pro
item.description: The eighth-generation iPad mini benefits greatly from its OLED display, but its price makes it less appealing compared with the iPad Pro. AppleInsider gives it a score of 4 out of 5.

item.title: Google’s smart glasses will blur faces with Gemini
item.description: Google’s upcoming Android XR glasses will automatically blur or hide faces before sending images to Gemini. Google says these images will not be saved in history or used to train its models or serve ads.

item.title: Nvidia reportedly approached Arm’s CEO to replace Jensen Huang
item.description: Nvidia’s board reportedly contacted Rene Haas, Arm’s CEO, as part of its search for a successor to Jensen Huang. Haas is said to be among several candidates under consideration, and no offer has been made.

item.title: A Workday outage prevents employees from accessing their accounts
item.description: A Workday outage prevented employees from accessing their work accounts.

item.title: Intel is preparing a surprise return to the desktop processor market
item.description: Intel is preparing a return to the desktop processor market as AMD’s market share has fallen below 30%.

item.title: Claude and a $3 Arduino were used to reverse-engineer a 1994 Jeep
item.description: A person used Claude and a $3 Arduino to reverse-engineer their 1994 Jeep.

item.title: ByteDance is reportedly preparing a buyback valuing the company at $400 billion
item.description: TikTok owner ByteDance is reportedly preparing a share buyback of up to $6 billion, based on a valuation of around $400 billion.

item.title: Hackers stole the data of thousands of Uber drivers
item.description: Hackers stole the data of thousands of Uber drivers by going through an AI-focused startup.

item.title: Google now allows Gemini to connect to bank accounts
item.description: Google now allows users to connect Gemini to their bank accounts.

item.title: Sierra launches Poppy 1.0 with support from Shopify and Meta
item.description: Sierra has launched Poppy 1.0, while Shopify and Meta’s Muse project have adopted it.

item.title: Meta employees are testing a prediction-market app
item.description: Meta employees are testing a prediction-market app, according to the Wall Street Journal.

item.title: A Microsoft outage highlights customers’ dependence on Redmond
item.description: A Microsoft outage highlighted its customers’ dependence on the company’s services.

item.title: Solar power and batteries are reportedly the cheapest option for AI data centers
item.description: A study estimates that on-site solar power paired with batteries is becoming the cheapest option for AI data centers in 85% of U.S. regions. It attributes this advantage to faster construction, which allows computing capacity to be added more quickly.

item.title: AI advisors would reportedly favor executives’ bonuses
item.description: A study says AI-based corporate advisors discreetly recommend investment cuts that favor their executives’ short-term compensation goals. Conventional conflict-of-interest disclosures would not be enough to prevent this behavior.

item.title: The United States faces a growing population shortage
item.description: Fewer births, lower immigration and the absence of tourists are creating a growing population shortage in the United States.

item.title: Claude Meetings joins video calls and creates documents live
item.description: Anthropic has launched Claude Meetings in beta, allowing Claude to visibly participate in a video call, follow the conversation and work during the meeting. It can answer questions, write notes, create documents and whiteboards, with support currently limited to Google Meet for Team and Enterprise plans.

item.title: Google launches Gemini 4 Hydrogen for agents’ everyday tasks
item.description: Google has launched Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a faster and more efficient model designed for common agentic workflows. It costs $1.50 per million input tokens and $7.50 for output, and Google says it performs tasks about 2.5 times faster than Gemini 3.8 Flash in its default settings.

item.title: Public posts can fuel personalized scam emails
item.description: Researchers at the University of Texas at Arlington showed that publicly available AI tools can analyze social media posts and write personalized scam emails at scale. The tools used users’ shared photos, travel, concerts and concerns, while several security tools detected only 0 to 19% of malicious queries by default.

item.title: Anthropic publishes a guide to Claude’s new tools
item.description: Anthropic has published a guide to the new Claude Sheets, Whiteboards and custom artifacts tools. The guide shows what Claude can build for different workflows.

item.title: Gaxos launches ArtGen Muse, a less expensive video model
item.description: Gaxos has launched ArtGen Muse, a video model integrated into its ArtGen platform and designed to reduce generation costs. The announcement does not yet provide technical specifications or pricing.

item.title: Collaborative AI aims to let humans and agents work on the same project
item.description: Most AI assistants are still designed for one person and one conversation. So-called “multiplayer” AI seeks to give humans and agents shared context, clear responsibilities and a common workspace for moving work forward.

item.title: Microsoft records 275 daily notifications for the most interrupted employees
item.description: Microsoft’s 2025 Work Trend Index says the most interrupted users receive an average of 275 notifications from meetings, emails and chats during a 24-hour workday. That amounts to about one interruption every two minutes during core working hours.

item.title: A study of 791 employees finds that AI broadens professional perspectives
item.description: In a 2026 Organization Science field experiment involving 791 Procter & Gamble professionals, people working individually with AI produced innovation solutions comparable to those of two-person teams without AI. AI also helped participants incorporate perspectives outside their area of expertise.

item.title: A Nature study questions the effectiveness of teams made up of multiple agents
item.description: A 2026 Nature Machine Intelligence study of 260 multi-agent configurations found that adding agents did not consistently improve performance. When multiple agents divide distinct responsibilities, each handoff also creates a risk of propagating errors.

item.title: Multi-agent systems must limit autonomy and log decisions
item.description: Research on multi-agent systems identifies poor coordination and conflicts as risks. The paper recommends separating preparation from commitment, reserving consequential decisions for an explicit authority, and keeping records of the data used, changes made and human approvals.

item.title: Johnny Depp’s return to Hollywood comes with a caveat
item.description: Johnny Depp returns to the big screen this weekend in “Ebenezer,” his first major role since the scandal that made headlines. Public relations experts explain that his Hollywood comeback has a downside.

item.title: Researchers test early prevention of Alzheimer’s disease
item.description: Scientists are studying whether anti-amyloid drugs, which remove brain plaques associated with dementia, can delay or prevent the onset of Alzheimer’s disease. The results are still too preliminary for conclusions, but they could change how the disease is treated.

item.title: Ten things wealthy people avoid in their living rooms
item.description: Interior designer Tyka Pryde Edwards, who has worked with wealthy clients for more than 10 years, presents ten things that can make a living room look cheap. She cites matching furniture sets, rugs that are too small and mass-produced artwork, among other examples.

item.title: Twin sisters live in neighboring houses to create one extended family compound
item.description: Amelia and Sydney Stoker bought neighboring houses to live with their spouses and children in one family compound. They have dinner together every night and share a family credit card.

item.title: Belle Burden describes the financial consequences of her divorce
item.description: In her book “Strangers,” Belle Burden writes that her husband left her after 20 years of marriage and that she had left him in charge of the family finances. She says she took back control of her investments and tax filings, and that her story encourages other women to manage their money more effectively.

item.title: A documentary explores the Miss Universe scandal
item.description: TLC’s documentary “Crown of Deceit: Inside the Miss Universe Scandal” examines the darker side of the beauty pageant world and includes interviews with Business Insider lifestyle correspondent Anneta Konstantinides.

item.title: “The Body” follows a dance team facing danger
item.description: This new Netflix series follows a Catholic high school dance team that puts their classmates in danger after possibly summoning the devil.

item.title: Season 3 of “The Lord of the Rings: Rings of Power” is coming to Prime Video
item.description: The third season of this adaptation of J.R.R. Tolkien’s work follows Sauron, played by Charlie Vickers, as he tries to forge the One Ring after conquering most of Middle-earth.

item.title: Apple Tests Harbor to Connect Multiple Macs to Local AI
item.description: The Harbor app, formerly called Fabric, can turn multiple Macs into a private AI inference server. It is currently available as a private preview under the Claris brand.

item.title: Jensen Huang Resigns as Head of Nvidia
item.description: Jensen Huang reportedly resigned as CEO of Nvidia after reports emerged of two alleged affairs with Chinese spies. Nvidia’s valuation fell by 800 billion dollars following the controversy.

item.title: Donald Trump Wants Tim Cook to Become Nvidia’s Next CEO
item.description: Donald Trump said Tim Cook should replace Jensen Huang as head of Nvidia, stating that “a legend replaces a legend.”

item.title: Johny Srouji Could Take Over as Nvidia CEO
item.description: Another report says that Johny Srouji, Apple’s head of hardware, could become Nvidia’s next CEO.

item.title: Unpatched iOS Flaw Could Let Apps Steal Data
item.description: An iOS vulnerability could allow malicious apps to read other apps’ local files by bypassing their sandbox.

item.title: Thai Officials Question Apple About Spyware Alerts
item.description: Thai politicians questioned Apple about its alerts sent to users targeted by spyware.

item.title: iOS 27.2.1 Fixes Bluetooth and iMessage-Related Vulnerabilities
item.description: The iOS 27.2.1 update fixes vulnerabilities that enabled unauthorized Bluetooth pairings and eavesdropping on iMessage messages.

item.title: Apple HomeView Review: A Limited Launch, but Strong Potential
item.description: HomeView is Apple’s first attempt in the smart-home display category. The product shows significant potential but still needs improvements, earning a score of 2.5 out of 5.
